title: arXiv Mathematics — 24 November 2026 batch: 8 notable new papers
global_caveat: This is an inferred shortlist, not an official arXiv trending chart. All selected signal scores arise from cross-listing; no direct attention score was found in the candidate records, and usable citation evidence is unavailable for this very recent batch. A zero score is not evidence of unimportance.

sections.title: Möbius Fusion Algebra
sections.abstract: For a pseudo-unitary modular tensor category with an anti-monoidal involution, the authors define a generally noncommutative Möbius fusion algebra and give a formula for dimensions of its simple modules.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the algebra is semisimple and identify its simple-module dimensions using the modular S-matrix and data from the involution; they interpret this as a non-orientable analogue of the Verlinde formula.
sections.signal: Three cross-lists (0.25 each); top-score tie. The arXiv comment links animated proof versions for two propositions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The input is a pseudo-unitary modular tensor category together with an anti-monoidal involution; the motivation is Reshetikhin–Turaev-type TQFT on non-orientable manifolds.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly do not construct the proposed non-orientable TQFT in full generality; the formula’s TQFT role remains an expected interpretation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three cross-lists (0.25 each); top-score tie. The arXiv comment links animated proof versions for two propositions.

sections.title: Strong holonomicity of functions on curves
sections.abstract: For a smooth affine irreducible complex curve, the authors show that a local solution-counting index of a differential operator equals the Calogero–Moser index of its Weyl closure, then apply it to annihilators of locally holomorphic functions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that the holonomicity index computed by counting solutions in truncated local rings at singular points equals the Calogero–Moser index of the Weyl closure; they use this to compute indices for selected function annihilators.
sections.signal: Three cross-lists (0.25 each); top-score tie. Its claimed equality connects a local differential-equation invariant to a geometric classification of operator ideals.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The main theorem concerns nonzero differential operators on a smooth affine irreducible curve over C and the corresponding global differential-operator ring.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper computes the invariant in selected examples rather than giving a universal closed formula for every holonomic function; its proposed colored-Jones extension is conjectural, not proved here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three cross-lists (0.25 each); top-score tie. Its claimed equality connects a local differential-equation invariant to a geometric classification of operator ideals.

sections.title: Neural Schrödinger Bridge via Yasue Action with Applications to Generative Modeling
sections.abstract: The authors propose a neural Schrödinger-bridge solver that learns a deterministic velocity field from endpoint samples through a saddle-point formulation using the Yasue action.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive a saddle-point formulation and report consistency for it, then demonstrate the method on synthetic and real data in low and high dimensions; the learned ODE velocity replaces the usual learned SDE drift.
sections.signal: Three cross-lists (0.25 each); top-score tie. Placed after tied algebraic results because the abstract reports a solver and numerical demonstrations rather than a structural theorem.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: It uses samples from source and target distributions rather than known density functions; the stated Schrödinger-bridge existence setting assumes finite second moments.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract supports effectiveness through numerical experiments, not a broad independent benchmark or a general performance guarantee over all generative tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three cross-lists (0.25 each); top-score tie. Placed after tied algebraic results because the abstract reports a solver and numerical demonstrations rather than a structural theorem.

sections.title: Deterministic regularisation of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem
sections.abstract: The author gives a deterministic exact-arithmetic algorithm that perturbs a complex contraction to a simple-spectrum matrix with controlled eigenbasis conditioning and computes the resulting eigensystem.
sections.claimed_result: For a complex contraction A of order n≥2 and 0<δ<1/2, the author claims a deterministic algorithm finding ||E||<δ such that A+E has simple spectrum, with the condition-number/minimum-gap ratio bounded by C(n/δ)^(20/3), using O(n^3 log^d(n/δ)) real-field operations and comparisons.
sections.signal: Two cross-lists (0.25 each); claimed resolution of an open complexity problem and explicit perturbation and operation bounds support placement within the score tier.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The guarantee is for complex contractions in exact arithmetic, with absolute constants C and d; the algorithm also computes an exact eigensystem of the perturbed matrix.
sections.unique_caveat: These bounds are stated for the contraction-and-perturbation setting, not as a uniform guarantee for every unmodified nonsymmetric eigenproblem.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Two cross-lists (0.25 each); claimed resolution of an open complexity problem and explicit perturbation and operation bounds support placement within the score tier.

sections.title: A Proof of Blackburn's Conjecture on Non-Overlapping Codes
sections.abstract: For non-overlapping codes of fixed length over large alphabets, the author proves Blackburn’s conjecture about optimal codes and characterizes the codes attaining Levenshtein’s bound.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves Blackburn’s conjecture: for every code length n and all sufficiently large alphabet sizes q, the best non-overlapping codes are maximum ones; the abstract also identifies the equality cases for Levenshtein’s bound.
sections.signal: Two cross-lists (0.25 each); explicit proof of a named conjecture and equality characterization make this a concrete result in the score tier.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Codewords have fixed length n over an alphabet of size q; “non-overlapping” means no nonempty proper prefix of a codeword is a suffix of a codeword.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract states an eventual-in-q result but does not give the threshold for “sufficiently large” q.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Two cross-lists (0.25 each); explicit proof of a named conjecture and equality characterization make this a concrete result in the score tier.

sections.title: The Gerards-Schrijver conjecture on the Edmonds-Johnson property is false
sections.abstract: The author disproves a proposed forbidden-minor characterization by constructing a minimal 5×6 totally half-modular matrix that violates the Edmonds–Johnson property but contains neither of the two conjectured minors.
sections.claimed_result: The author gives a 5×6 counterexample with no minor equal to either of the two specified matrices, and proves it is minimal by reducing every proper minor to known classes with the property.
sections.signal: Two cross-lists (0.25 each); explicit minimal counterexample and proof that every proper minor has the property provide concrete progress on the conjecture.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The statement concerns totally half-modular integral matrices and the equality of the first Chvátal closure with the integer hull for the specified bounded systems.
sections.unique_caveat: This refutes the proposed characterization; it does not supply a replacement classification of all matrices with the Edmonds–Johnson property.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Two cross-lists (0.25 each); explicit minimal counterexample and proof that every proper minor has the property provide concrete progress on the conjecture.

sections.title: Reduction types of curves in tame extensions
sections.abstract: For curves over discretely valued fields, the author gives sufficient conditions under which a tame base extension determines the curve’s reduction type, along with an algorithm for possible types using harmonic graph covers.
sections.claimed_result: Under sufficient conditions on the original reduction type R and a tame extension degree n, the new reduction type is uniquely determined; the author also gives an algorithm for possible types and a characterization of tame curves with potentially good reduction.
sections.signal: Two cross-lists (0.25 each); connects arithmetic geometry with graph combinatorics and provides a reduction-type algorithm and a characterization of potentially good reduction.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: C/K has genus at least one over a discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field; the extension L/K is finite and tame. The abstract highlights zero abelian and toric ranks as a case satisfying the sufficient conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: Outside the stated sufficient conditions, the result is an algorithm for possibilities rather than a uniqueness theorem for every reduction type.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Two cross-lists (0.25 each); connects arithmetic geometry with graph combinatorics and provides a reduction-type algorithm and a characterization of potentially good reduction.

sections.title: Improved Lower Bound on the Hadwiger-Debrunner Numbers
sections.abstract: The author improves asymptotic lower bounds for the Hadwiger–Debrunner piercing numbers using parallelotopes and the hypergraph container method.
sections.claimed_result: For d≥2 the author proves HD_d(p,d+1)≥p^(d−o(1)), and more generally HD_d(p,q)≥p^((q−1)/(q−d)−o(1)); the bound is tight up to polylogarithmic factors among families with bounded VC dimension.
sections.signal: One cross-list (0.25), weaker cross-list proxy than the higher-ranked entries; selected for explicit asymptotic exponents on a longstanding extremal-geometric problem.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The setting is the (p,q)-theorem for families of convex sets in R^d, with p≥q≥d+1; the stated tightness comparison is restricted to bounded-VC-dimension families.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound is asymptotic and does not determine the exact Hadwiger–Debrunner numbers; the bounded-VC tightness statement is not a claim of tightness for all convex-set families.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: One cross-list (0.25), weaker cross-list proxy than the higher-ranked entries; selected for explicit asymptotic exponents on a longstanding extremal-geometric problem.
